_comment: The project coverage slot registry. Data, not code: the wording of a
question must never mean touching a schema or a state machine.
This is the project-level counterpart of slots.json. The difference is not
size but subject: slots.json interrogates one idea, this one interrogates
an architecture somebody has already written. Most slots are therefore
`fact` and answerable from that architecture — a question put to the
Product Owner about something they already wrote down is a question that
Question order is the topological order of depends_on, ties broken by the
order of this list. That is what makes the interview reproducible for a
lookup_first names the cheap sources consulted before anyone's attention
is spent. `architecture` is the document the Product Owner supplied and is
always the first place to look.

slots.closes_when: what the system is and whose problem it solves are stated without naming components
what is inside the system and what is deliberately outside it are both stated
every component is named and carries one clause of what it is responsible for
every interaction carries a direction and a protocol; an arrow with neither is not an interaction
every piece of data has exactly one component that owns it
every external system is named together with what happens when it is absent
every component is assigned to a unit that is deployed as a whole
at least one end-to-end scenario is named in the user's words, not in components
the constraints that were not chosen freely are stated — platform, budget, organisation, law
what the system will not do is stated; an empty non-goals list is refused, never defaulted
